name: Palette The Travellers Hotel Bangkok
detail: The MRT is quiet and peaceful, but it's a bit hard to find food. It's about 300 meters away from 7-Eleven. I couldn't use the Wi-Fi both nights. The air conditioning is very cold. The hot water is warm to the point of being hot. Overall, it's worth it.

name: Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Bangkok
detail: I used it when traveling to the Queen Sirikit Convention Center. It is directly connected to BTS Asok / MRT Sukhumvit station. When you get off at the station, there are arrows pointing to the hotel above, which is convenient as you can reach the convention center without getting wet from the rain. The station is also directly connected to Terminal 21, making it easy to find places to eat. The room wasn't large, but it was spacious for a Japanese-style hotel, and it was comfortable with good facilities. The staff are also very friendly. (There are staff members who speak Korean!) I haven't had the chance to use the breakfast, bar, or pool.

name: Palette Hi Hotel Bangkok
detail: Room with a good location Review of a room that is beautiful, clean, and offers great value. There are various types and sizes of rooms to choose from, ranging from standard rooms to executive suites, which are very spacious, perfect for relaxing whether you're here for work, a getaway with a partner, family, or hanging out with friends. It's very convenient for traveling, close to shopping malls, the sky train, fresh markets, and night markets. Importantly, the staff here are friendly, polite, and provide excellent service. Highly recommended! Hi Hotel Bangkok ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐🥰🥰

name: The Landmark Bangkok
detail: This was a last-minute booking due to a flight delay, but it turned out to be the kindest and most comfortable place among the three accommodations I stayed at during this trip. Although it's an older establishment and not a trendy new hotel or an Instagram-worthy spot, the details of older Bangkok hotels that can’t be seen in newer ones are great, and the service from the staff is very comforting. In fact, it’s not uncommon to encounter expensive places where faucets splash a lot, toilets are too high, or amenities that feel overpriced and barely useful. However, here everything felt just right, not too little and not too much, tailored perfectly for guests. They allowed early check-in two hours before our scheduled time and offered late check-out at 4 PM. Additionally, you can enjoy cocktails and a variety of finger foods for free while watching the night view from the 31st-floor lounge. The swimming pool is 2.6 meters deep... Later, I borrowed some tape for my luggage, and they were more than happy to lend it. Thanks to Clovis at the reception, I was well-fed with a really delicious latte, complete with rich milk foam, and I arrived at the airport with ample time to spare. It's located right in front of Nana Station, making it easy to go anywhere, and I was truly disappointed to have only spent one night there. The breakfast might not have a wide variety, but it is prepared with care rather than just relying on seasonings, and the coffee is absolutely the best. Sipping coffee while gazing at the skyscrapers in the morning made me not want to go home. I recommend this place to those who miss classic hotel service. The lounge view of the city is stunning, so skip the rooftop bar and come here instead!

name: Mode Sathorn Hotel
detail: It is a very beautiful and luxurious hotel with a good atmosphere and a pleasant scent throughout. The staff provides good service, there is a welcome drink, and the swimming pool is beautiful. The Business Studio room is extremely beautiful and well-decorated, with a clear glass that overlooks the city. The hot water flows well. I will definitely come back to stay again.

name: The Quart Ruamrudee by UHG
detail: I made a reservation because it's close to Lumpini Park. The pool is modest and the gym is very small, so you should consider it almost non-existent (just for running). The running is better at the nearby Lumpini Park.

name: Four Wings Hotel
detail: I always stay here in Bangkok. It's a bit far from the main station, but it's walkable (it might be a bit far with a suitcase). It's about 15 minutes away. I use a motorbike taxi, so it's 5 minutes for me. The hotel has been renovated and is clean everywhere. There is a pool, a gym, and a sauna, so the facilities are more than satisfactory. There is a convenience store and a supermarket close by, so it's convenient. The prices are low, so I am very satisfied.

name: NANA Hotel Bangkok
detail: We stayed for three nights with two women starting March 30. We hoped for twin beds and messaged multiple times through Agoda, but received no response. When we checked in, prepared to sleep in a double bed with my friend, we were happily surprised to find a proper twin room waiting for us on the renovated 11th floor. The room was clean, spacious, and the air conditioning worked very well. Don’t forget to tip the hotel staff who help carry your luggage and the ones who clean the room every day. Everyone at the hotel was kind and friendly, and I really liked the older male staff member at the front desk in the evening who was very funny! The hotel location was very easy to find, right in front of NANA Plaza, which was lively until morning and perfect for those who enjoy nightlife. It felt safe even for women. There are many places to shop around, and you can find cheap souvenirs at the underground part of Nana Square. The breakfast was also free and very satisfactory. However, there were no room wear and slippers provided, so you must bring your own. The water pressure in the shower was fine, and they provided enough bottles of mineral water for each person every day, so we didn’t have to buy any! We initially planned to move around by taxi using Grab throughout our trip, but since the station was only about a 5-minute walk away, we used the train instead. It was cheap, clean, and comfortable, so I recommend it. I’m really glad our first trip to Thailand was at this hotel. I will definitely stay here again when I come to Thailand in the future. Thank you!

name: Asia Hotel Bangkok
detail: It's a large hotel with a luxurious lobby. My friend and I stayed in a twin room, and it was about 5,000 yen per person per night including breakfast. The room was spacious enough, and we slept very well. When we went for breakfast early in the morning, the bakery on the first floor had bread that was really delicious. The chocolate cake and the small bread topped with sesame were also tasty. It's directly connected to the BTS, making it easy to travel, and you can find local restaurants and reasonably priced massage shops near the hotel. There was no toothbrush in the room, the hotel is large so the room was far away, it was extremely crowded around 9 AM on Sunday when we went for breakfast, and the air conditioning adjustment was basic (no air volume adjustment), so keep these in mind. It was a great stay for my first time in Bangkok.

name: W 21 HOTEL Bangkok
detail: The accommodation is clean, tastefully and modernly decorated. The room is compact but has quite a complete range of amenities, including a water heater, hairdryer, TV, air purifier, under-bed storage, and a wooden wardrobe. The bathroom is clean; it would be perfect if there were a clothes rack in the bathroom. It's close to MRT and BTS, next to a 7-Eleven, and all the staff including security and housekeeping are friendly.
